purpose: Ganciclovir is used to treat a viral infection called CMV (cytomegalovirus), which can cause serious eye infections that may lead to blindness, especially in people with weakened immune systems such as those with HIV/AIDS or organ transplant recipients. It can also be used to prevent CMV infections in people who have had an organ transplant. The eye gel form is used to treat a CMV infection in the eye called retinitis.
how_it_works: Ganciclovir works by blocking the virus from making copies of itself inside your body. It basically gets in the way of the virus's ability to reproduce and spread. This gives your immune system a better chance to fight off the infection and helps keep the virus under control.
common_side_effects: Low blood cell counts which can make you tired, more prone to infections, or cause easy bruising or bleeding. You may also experience nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, loss of appetite, fever, or headache. Some people notice kidney problems or feel generally weak or unwell.
warnings: This medication can seriously lower your white blood cells, red blood cells, and platelets, so regular blood tests are very important while taking it. It may harm an unborn baby, so both men and women should use reliable birth control during treatment and for some time after. Ganciclovir may also affect fertility. Do not take it if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant without talking to your doctor first. Avoid contact with people who are sick, and tell your doctor right away if you notice unusual bleeding, bruising, signs of infection like fever or chills, or changes in urination.
typical_dosing: For serious CMV infections, the usual adult intravenous (IV) dose is 5 mg per kilogram of body weight given twice daily for 2 to 3 weeks to get the infection under control, followed by once-daily dosing to keep it from coming back. For the eye gel form, one drop is placed in the affected eye five times a day until the ulcer heals, then three times a day for one week. Your doctor will adjust your dose based on your kidney function and how you respond to treatment.
